Interface JwtPayloadRepository

public interface JwtPayloadRepository
Repository abstraction for issuing, verifying and parsing JSON Web Tokens within the easy-4-java security stack.

All methods on this interface are default so that implementations can pick the level of indirection they want to expose. The base methods are intentionally permissive — by default an empty string is returned for every issue operation and false for every verify operation — allowing callers to use the repository as a no-op during early integration.

  • Method Details

    • issueJwt

      default String issueJwt(org.springframework.security.authentication.AbstractAuthenticationToken token)
      Issue a JWT for the SecurityPrincipal carried by the supplied authentication token.

      If the token's principal is not a SecurityPrincipal, an empty string is returned. The default implementation simply delegates to issueJwt(SecurityPrincipal).

      Parameters:
      token - the Spring Security authentication token
      Returns:
      the encoded JWT, or an empty string if no principal is present

    • issueJwt

      default String issueJwt(SecurityPrincipal principal)
      Issue a JWT for the supplied principal. By default delegates to issueJwt(String, Map) using the principal's uid and profile.
      Parameters:
      principal - the security principal
      Returns:
      the encoded JWT

    • issueJwt

      default String issueJwt(String uid, Map<String,Object> profile)
      Issue a JWT for the supplied user id and profile map.

      The default implementation returns an empty string; concrete repositories are expected to override it.

      Parameters:
      uid - the upstream user id
      profile - the profile map to embed as claims
      Returns:
      the encoded JWT

    • getProfilePayload

      default UserProfilePayload getProfilePayload(org.springframework.security.authentication.AbstractAuthenticationToken token, boolean checkExpiry)
      Build a UserProfilePayload for the principal carried by the supplied authentication token and decorate it with a freshly-issued JWT.

      The default implementation casts the token's principal to SecurityPrincipal, calls SecurityPrincipal.toPayload(), embeds the freshly-issued token via issueJwt(AbstractAuthenticationToken) and returns the resulting payload.

      Parameters:
      token - the Spring Security authentication token
      checkExpiry - whether the expiration should be checked when issuing
      Returns:
      a profile payload populated with the freshly-issued JWT
